title: Charcoal Briquettes 8kg

drivers.name: Price increase (5.3%)
drivers.evidence: Historical 30% discount drove x2.53 lift; 5.3% price increase likely reduces demand. No past price hike shows lift. Noise-adjusted effect of similar price change is x1.0, but directional logic suggests downside.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 37.2. No events are scheduled. The price is up 5.3% to $15.96, which likely reduces demand. Past price increases (e.g., Easter week) show no lift; in fact, the 30% discount in April 2026 drove a strong spike (x2.53), suggesting price sensitivity. A 5.3% increase is unlikely to boost demand. The noise-adjusted effect of Mother's Day is x1.0, so no uplift. The classical model suggests no change, which aligns with evidence. No promotion or event justifies adjustment. Downside risk from price hike is credible. Spread widened slightly due to price uncertainty.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-67% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
